lexicalLimitations: Regex checks bounded English clause windows ([^.\n;]) and common singular/verb path tokens; multi-sentence cross-clause contradictions separated by periods or uncommon irregular singular paths (e.g. /person) are not parsed semantically.

Irregular plurals not ending in 's' (e.g. /people, /children) and singular nouns ending in 's' outside the explicit exclusion list (status, alias, basis, focus) can produce false negatives or false positives.

lexicalLimitations: Top-level verb-in-path detection targets enumerated action verbs paired with common domain nouns (order, product, user, item, payment, invoice, account, customer, subscription) because checkAssertion compiles regexes case-insensitively ('i' flag) and cannot rely on camelCase boundaries alone.

Any 3-segment route matching /resource/:id/segment can satisfy a2 as an action sub-resource route; semantic distinction between an action sub-resource (/orders/:id/cancel) and a 3-segment nested child singleton is outside regex scope.
